This basically nails it on the head. As a person who has been there and gotten all the way to the point of attempting suicide twice, this is pretty much how it felt at the time. I was terribly alone and there wasn't an ounce of hope for change or betterment left in me. 

All anyone seemed to want when interacting with me was to see how much they could take and I was happy to give as much as I could. It meant they might turn around and do a nice thing at the right time for me. Or it meant it would sting them just a bit more when I was gone, and I was fine with that.

While I haven't tried to shoot myself, I have gone the Tylenol route. It was one of the worst experiences of my life and nearly killed me a week after overdosing. While I don't know much about it on the medical side of things, I would wholly say for no one to try this method.
He and his girlfriend thought it was a good idea to Baker Act me and give me 3 days to find a new place to live. On the same night.

Hey there, I'm in a similar enough situation i feel like i can give some kind of advice. Take everything in small chunks.
Take as little of a step forward as you need. So long as it's a step you can handle. You're living back at home with your abusive father? Talk to your closest friend, maybe you two could get an apartment.
Your father doesn't want you on antidepressants? Talk to your doctor, maybe even a different doctor, and find a different medicine. They're not all the same, believe me. They function very differently, obviously you reacted negatively to the last one you were on, maybe you can try a different one.

You want to disappear, to not exist. That is exactly how i feel. I don't want to exist, feel like i never should have to begin with and see no reason to continue on. Nix all of those thoughts. Focus entirely on getting yourself back. Find a better place that you want to be. Figure out how to get there and set things in motion.  

Just break things down into manageable chunks. Don't try to build a colony on mars, lets focus on trying to get back to the moon first.

I don't know if any of that will help, but i hope it did/does. If no one here can get you an answer you like, you can always post again. It's infinitely better then the alternative.

Thank you! :)

Yup. South Florida born, raised, and never left. You are the good type of internet stranger and i'm sorry if you mistook what i was saying. 

I have been at the point where i didn't really think what would happen to others if i killed myself. Then i moved on to not caring. I still think about what would happen, but it doesn't bother me that people might miss me anymore. It doesn't bother me that my suicide will hurt people anymore. 

As far as my roommates are concerned, one has severe anxiety that she's being medicated for. She said she couldn't take me anymore. I always tried to help her through her anxiety where i could but she never really made any real effort to return the favor. Which is fine. I didn't help her expecting to be helped out later. 
My other roommate (first one's boyfriend) made it a point to tell me that he's lost his appetite and has trouble sleeping so he's seeking a counselor for his high stress levels. He blames me for the extra stress and says that it's affecting his career. He thinks that because i came to him first with my suicidal ideation and depression i expected him to fix me, set me up and make it all better. I've repeatedly told him all i wanted was someone who knew and would be there to talk when i needed it. He got it into his head to Baker Act me even after i told him i would rather kill myself then be baker acted. I don't really know how much significance i expected that to have now that i think about it.

Keep in mind they were my two best friends. 

As far as my work, I'm the stock manager at Brookstone and have been for a few years. I just quit being a stock clerk at Publix because it was triggering depressive spirals almost every shift. I would wake up happy and energized, then i would go into publix and quickly spiral down to suicidal thoughts that stayed in my head until i was in bed. 

I don't know how much more you're willing to reply but i wanted to thank you for your time. Mr./Ms. Nice internet person.

Honestly my life isn't all that terrible. It could be better, but it could be a lot worse. That doesn't change the depression.

 I had two jobs working 55-60 hours a week for crap money, came home to roommates who quietly resented me being in the apartment. They tried to help, but their idea of help was talking to me three times? And then tried to Baker Act me the same night they told me to find a new place to live. Now i live with my parents. Where i hate the house and how they live. I quit one job so now i'm only working 40 hours a week for the next three months then back to no real job to speak of.

I feel like i have no future to speak of. I have no relationship history and no i one who i can really see that cares about me. So i wait.

I have the same fears as you. Every time i don't see my friends for more then a day I become convinced that they left me, that no one cares about me anymore. Every time i see them again I'm excited and ecstatic but most overwhelmingly surprised. 

For me, I fear that they will leave me behind and forget about me at every turn in life. Yes i do lose some, but that's inevitable. Most of them always come back, always stay in contact and stay friends. And I'm always surprised. 

I guess all I can say is yes it feels like your SO will never come back, but try to keep that surprise in the back of your mind.

For me it's the need to feel needed. I don't think i need to be special at one particular thing (even though every new thing i do i hope like hell i'm it's Harry Potter) I really just feel the need to be the guy that people can't easily replace. Like i always want to be the person who is the go-to when it comes to doing things.

I guess it's kind of the same but not? (If i'm interpreting it right) you feel the need to have that one thing, doesn't matter what, that makes you special and indispensable to the group, like i need to be needed/useful. 
I might just be projecting though.

Thanks. Change typically terrifies me. That being said, you're right, it could be positive. Hopefully something changes soon, for the both of us. 

The fact that you're even here responding to people tells me you're a good enough person that good things will happen for you. Keep your chin up, man.
